test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The role of the preparation of the electoral rolls for all the elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice-President lies with the ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Election Commission__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Election Commission**__

__
 
• On January 25, 1950, the Election Commission of India was constituted in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• Election Commission of India:
 
 
• The Election Commission of India is a permanent and autonomous body constituted by the Indian Constitution to ensure free and fair elections.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is a self-governing constitutional body that regulates the election process in India.
 
• The Constitution of India (Article 324) has vested in the Election Commission of India the superintendence, direction, and control of the entire process for conduct of elections to Parliament and Legislature of every State and the offices of President and Vice-President of India.
 
• Initially, there was only one Chief Election Commissioner on the board. There are currently two Election Commissioners and a Chief Election Commissioner.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet**

 
 
• The total number of ministers in the Cabinet, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Article 75 1(A) states that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of the People.
 
• Also, all ministers must be members of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission**
 
 
• The Finance Commission is a Constitutionally mandated body that is at the center of fiscal federalism. 
 
• Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides for a Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial body.
 
• It is constituted by the President of India every fifth year or at such earlier time as he considers necessary. 
 
• N.K. Singh is the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission of India.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission **​
 
 
• The Planning Commission, although no longer active (since it was replaced by the NITI Aayog), was an important feature of policymaking and governance in India.
 
• The Planning Commission was reporting directly to the Prime Minister of India.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India, on the recommendation of the Advisory Planning Board constituted in 1946, under the chairman of KC Neogi. Thus the Planning Commission was neither constitutional nor a statutory body. It was an advisory body. 
 
• It is a non-constitutional (not created by the Constitution) and a non-statutory body (not created by an act of Parliament).
